text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your upper arms, and tell me when it first started?

text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. speaker: Doctor
text: The rash sounds persistent and itchy. Can you describe the specific appearance of the lesions, such as whether they are raised bumps, patches, or blisters, and do they appear symmetrical on both arms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the lesions have a rough, sandpaper-like texture, and are they primarily located on the extensor surfaces of your arms? I would also like to know if you have any personal or family history of asthma, hay fever, or eczema.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No history of serious illness. No known drug allergies. Takes no medications. Social history: College student studying graphic design. Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since the rash is on the extensor surfaces and you have no history of atopy, I need to rule out other causes. Do you experience any pain or tendness in the muscles of your arms or shoulders, and have you noticed any muscle weakness or changes in your skin color, such as a violet hue or scaling?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fever, joint pains, weight loss, or changes in bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have denied muscle weakness and systemic symptoms, which makes inflammatory myopathy less likely. Given the chronic, pruritic nature of the rash on the extensor surfaces of a young adult, I suspect lichen planus. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lichen Planus
